conversation.content:
Hi there—I'm so glad we’re meeting today. My name is Claire, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I specialize in caring for new mothers, and I’m here to help make sure you’re feeling as supported as possible during this postpartum time.

I’d like to do a quick check-in using a tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—often just called the **EPDS**. It’s a short, 10-question form that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past seven days. It covers things like mood, anxiety, and, briefly, thoughts of self-harm. Because many moms experience big emotional swings after delivery, this gives us a snapshot of whether extra support or resources might help.

Your answers are completely confidential; anything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team providing your care. We’ll go at your pace, and you can pause or stop at any time. Each question just needs your honest sense of how things have been for you lately—no right or wrong answers.

Ready to begin? I’ll re-phrase the questions in everyday language, and we’ll keep things conversational.

**First question:** Over the last seven days, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you smile, or has that sense of enjoyment slipped away?

[soft sigh, eyes down for a second]

I… I can still enjoy *some* things, like when the baby finally latches right or when my toddler laughs, but it’s way less than before. Most of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Even the smell of my favorite coffee or a cute outfit doesn’t give me that little lift it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really… I mean, I’ll smile if my older kid does something silly, but I haven’t actually laughed in days. It feels like there’s this heavy blanket over everything, so even when something’s funny, it doesn’t reach me the way it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[slow head-shake]

Hardly anything. I used to get excited about little outings—like even a walk to the mailbox felt like a treat—but now it’s mostly dread or just… nothing. I still force myself to plan, because the kids need it, but I don’t feel that happy buzz I used to when I thought about going to the farmers’ market or having coffee with a friend.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a lot of the time. If the baby’s fussy, my brain jumps straight to “I’m not making enough milk,” or if the toddler has a meltdown I think, “If I were a better mom he wouldn’t act like this.” I know rationally it’s not all on me, but the guilt keeps popping up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes… pretty much every day. My heart races and my mind spins off with “what-ifs” about the baby—like if he’s still breathing every time he’s quiet in the bassinet. There’s no real reason, but I can’t shake the fear something awful is about to happen.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes I’ll be folding laundry and suddenly feel like I can’t breathe—like a wave of panic out of nowhere. It’s happened two or three times this week. Nothing’s wrong, but my chest gets tight and I have to sit down and count my breaths so I don’t spiral.
Things have been getting on top of me

[mouth twists, eyes well up a little]

Yeah… most days I feel like I’m drowning. The dishes pile up, the baby wants to nurse again, the toddler’s begging for snacks, and I just stand there frozen, thinking, “I literally can’t do all of this.” I still get through it, but it’s like clawing my way out instead of just handling it like I used to.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

[sighs, rubbing tired eyes]

Yes… most nights. I finally get the baby down, but then I lie there staring at the ceiling with all these thoughts spinning—did I sanitize the pump parts, is he gaining enough weight, will I ever feel like myself again? It takes me over an hour to fall asleep, and even when I do, I jolt awake at every little grunt from the bassinet.
I have felt sad or miserable

[shoulders slump]

Pretty much every day this week. It’s like a gray cloud that follows me around. I’ll be changing the baby and suddenly feel tears prick my eyes for no clear reason. I’m not crying all day, but there’s this heavy, sad weight in my chest that won’t lift.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[Voice cracks a little]

Yeah… I’ve broken down twice this week. Once was in the shower—everyone finally asleep, and I just slid to the floor and sobbed. The other time was yesterday when I couldn’t get the stroller unfolded; it felt like the stupidest thing to cry over, but I couldn’t stop the tears.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[eyes drop to hands clasped tightly in lap]

A couple of times… just quick flashes. Like when I’m rocking the baby at 3 a.m. and everything feels hopeless, I’ll think, “What if I just didn’t wake up?” I haven’t made any plans and I know I’d never leave my kids, but those thoughts pop in for a second or two and scare me.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 27: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

Demographic: Postpartum mother, exact weeks post-birth not specified.  
Screening tool: Clinician-guided EPDS-style interview.  

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, inability to laugh or look forward to activities (Q1-2)  
- Daily crying spells, subjective “gray cloud,” tearfulness with routine tasks (Q8-9)  
- Pathologic guilt / self-blame regarding infant care and toddler behavior (Q3)  
- Anxious preoccupation, racing heart, “what-ifs” about infant safety (Q4)  
- Episodic panic symptoms: sudden breathlessness, chest tightness 2–3×/week (Q5)  
- Overwhelmed/drowning sensation, task paralysis (Q6)  
- Mood-congruent insomnia: initial and maintenance difficulties despite infant sleep (Q7)  

**Pattern**  
Symptoms present “pretty much every day this week,” causing functional impairment with childcare and self-care.  

**Risk factors**  
- Sleep deprivation linked to mood disturbance  
- High parenting-related guilt and self-criticism  
- Recurrent intrusive thoughts of not waking up / fleeting passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent (Q10) → **Safety concern**  

**Screening significance**  
Findings consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depressive and anxiety symptoms; rule-out major depressive episode with peripartum onset and comorbid anxiety disorder. Safety evaluation warranted given presence of self-harm ideation.  

*(Screening only; formal diagnosis and treatment planning to follow comprehensive evaluation.)*
